title: WHOA Hot Mama
text:
WHOA Hot Mama. Wow. I have been using an induction burner for about 1.5 years. Background: a crummy kitchenette in an old apt with an old inefficient electric stove where all the burners are shot. I had been quite pleased with my old induction burner (nat'l store brand) for all this time. It was about 1300 watts. On Thanksgiving weekend the fan which under normal conditions is rather noisy started making a racket I associate with shot bearings in computer fans that will fail shortly. So I ordered up this baby figuring I had something that was going to fail in the near future.

I knew going in that this thing was more powerful than my faithful old friend here by specs alone but had quite the demonstration tonight when it seared two small frozen chuck fillets in a cast iron pan. It seared them on like 3 on the heat/wattage setting.

One pet peeve: I do a considerable amount of cooking in a Fagor quality pressure cooker. On my old cooktop I had to keep it on a 3 setting and occasionally bump it up to 4 to keep pressure. Thinking about this one's settings I am pretty sure my PS will be sitting on it mostly 1 or at the very most a 2 setting.

Did some more cooking on it this morning, still using cast iron. I cannot go above a 5 with even my highest smoke point oil - rice bran oil. Couldn't lower it fast enough, got the pan near the control panel and it melted the panel. I am going to talk with Amazon, either my unit is defective or this thing is just way too hot. Half power - 900 watts? shouldn't be so hot that it can warp cast iron (my 75 year old pan!) and ignite rice bran oil. Also, the induction coil itself was obviously off-center. You can see where the coil is when you are boiling something, you will get the bubbles from where the coil is. This was off center badly enough that no way would I be able to use a 10inch pan without it too near the delicate control panel. Sent back.

product_metadata.title: Duxtop 1800W Portable Induction Cooktop Countertop Burner, Gold 8100MC/BT-180G3
features: Duxtop Induction Cooktop uses 120V 15 amp electrical outlet - standard in all North American homes; lightweight and compact for easy handling and storage.
Digital control panel. Built-in count-down digital timer with 1 minute increments up to 170 minutes; 10 temperature range from 140 °F to 460 °F; 10 power levels from 200 to 1800 Watts.

With no open flame or heating element, food does not burn-on the glass cooktop so this induction burner is easy to clean—just wipe with a damp towel. Durable 7-blade fan rapidly dissipates heat to ensure a longer product life.
The auto-pan detection will shut the unit automatically after 60 seconds if no cookware is detected; equipped with diagnostic error message system, low and high voltage warning system; ETL approved.

Note: In order to use this and any other induction stove, you need to use cookware with a magnetic bottom, whose diameter is at least 5 inches. 2-year manufacturer's warranty, as well as customer service.
